title: The Path of Chivalry
summary: Paladins who see knighthood as their kind's salvation.

claims.text: The mortal age of chivalry is only beginning, yet some Cainites, called Paladins, have embraced its ideals as the salvation of their kind.
It is one of the newer paths of the Road of Kings and has spread fast through the Cainite courts of Europe.

Nearly every Scion on the path hopes to join a knightly order; many such orders exist, most founded by Paladins or by Scions who saw their use, and some knights vow not to see the sun again until a duty is done, the freeing of the Holy Land being a favourite.

title: Tyrants of the Road of Kings
summary: Scions who want obedience without obligation.

claims.text: Tyrants grasp the worth of vassals and oaths of fealty but care little for responsibility or noblesse oblige.
They mock the Paladins' ideals as foolish and naive and hold that the strong owe nothing to those beneath them.

title: Scions of the Counting House
summary: A rising faction that backs merchants and craftsmen.

claims.text: While princes fight for domains, a small faction of Scions is quietly growing by seeing the promise in Europe's new class of merchants and skilled craftsmen.
To them money-lending is a minor sin next to the damnation already laid on Caine's children, and a loan to a desperate prince buys real power.

title: Scion Cults
summary: Followings the Scions gather around a lord or a bloodline.

claims.text: Mithras, Prince of London and undead king of England, took over the Cult of Mithras long ago and wears the god's name and identity.
Mithras holds none of the cult's beliefs, but it suits the Methuselah well for recruiting soldiers, the main focus of Mithras's attention.
Other Scion cults exist to preserve particular noble families or bloodlines.

title: Oaths of Fealty
summary: What a Scion owes a vassal and how a broken oath is felt.

claims.text: A liege's oath to a vassal is as sacred as the vassal's oath to the liege; a Scion who enforces an oath through the blood bond or Dominate takes on responsibility for that vassal.
Scions who treat others as pawns and discard them earn a bad name.

When a vassal breaks an oath of fealty, the Storyteller secretly rolls the liege's Perception + Leadership against the oathbreaker's Willpower; more successes reveal more, from the bare fact of the betrayal up to the oathbreaker's whereabouts and identity.

title: Assamite Viziers and the Road of Kings
summary: How the road looks in Haqim's clan.

claims.text: Many of the Assamite vizier caste follow a form of the road that treats Haqim's teachings on gathering power and control as its core.
Some Assamite princes who rule openly follow the road much as Europeans do, but subtlety is so prized in the clan that even they temper it.
